GTK Cyber Overview • This module will introduce you to vectorized data structures and the Pandas library. • You will learn how to explore tabular data sets. • Pandas 3.x

GTK Cyber A Word On Vibe Coding... • We fully expect (and encourage) you to use AI to generate the answers to the labs and exercises. • However, understanding the structure and mechanism of Pandas will allow you to give better direction to AI. • We therefore would suggest writing code manually until you are comfortable with the concepts behind Pandas. • Don't just cut/paste the instructions into an LLM.

GTK Cyber Why do this at all? • While you *can* send data to an LLM, there are issues with doing so: • There are fundamental limits as to how much data you can send to an LLM. • Analyzing data with an LLM is slow and costly. • No way to independently audit or verify the results. • LLMs can and will produce inaccurate information.

GTK Cyber A Better Approach with AI • Include a description of the data's schema and perhaps a sample in your AI prompt. • Have the LLM generate python code to accomplish your task • More on this later...

GTK Cyber Statistics: objectives This section will cover basic statistical methods commonly used in cleaning, analyzing and visualization of data. The relationship between statistics and data science will be discussed. The python skills learned thus far will be used to practice translating a mathematical equation into code. 1. Explain the difference between and calculate mean, median, mode, range, standard deviation, variance of a dataset 2. Differentiate when and why it is appropriate to use mean vs median 3. Use a histogram and box plot to understand the distribution of a dataset 4. Identify outliers and decide what actions to take 5. Normalize and scale a feature and describe when and why it is necessary
GTK Cyber Statistics: define Probability is a mathematical tool used to study randomness. It deals with the chance (the likelihood) of an event occurring

GTK Cyber Statistics: define Population - a collection of persons, things, or objects under study. To study the population, we select a sample - a portion (or subset) of the larger population. Study this portion (sample) to gain information about the population. Data are the result of sampling from a population. sample population

GTK Cyber Statistics: variables Variables - a characteristic or measurement for each member of a population Numerical - numbers (weight, bytes, time) Categorical - a category that members can be put into (user/bot, location)

GTK Cyber Statistics: types of data QuaLitative - aka categorical data, non-numeric data (user status, url, gender) QuanTitative - numeric data Discrete - integers, like the result of counting (# of site visits, log ins) Continuous - decimal numbers, fractions (weight, amount of time)

GTK Cyber Intro Stats: Covariance Covariance, like the variance, is a measure of spread, however it also measures how closely two datasets track each other. • Covariance is a squared quantity, so it is not on the same scale as the mean • Covariance of different pairs of variables can have completely different scales

GTK Cyber Tukey 5 Number Summary • Minimum: The smallest value in the dataset • Lower Quartile: Smallest 25% of the dataset • The Median: The middle value of the dataset • Upper Quartile: The largest 25% of the dataset • Maximum: The largest value in the dataset

GTK Cyber Intro Stats: IQR The interquartile range is a measure of where the “middle fifty” is in a data set. Where a range is a measure of where the beginning and end are in a set, an interquartile range is a measure of where the bulk of the values lie. http://www.statisticshowto.com/probability-and-statistics/interquartile- range/ IQR = data.quantile(0.75) - data.quantile(0.25)

GTK Cyber Scaling Pandas • Pandas is limited by the amount of memory on your machine. You will need 5-10x as much RAM as the size of your datasets. • Operations on DataFrames creates copies of the data in memory. • Pandas 3.0 is a major improvement in speed!

GTK Cyber Scaling Pandas Several drop-in or near drop-in replacements for Pandas exist that run on GPUs or parallelize operations. • Dask: A partial Pandas replacement geared towards running code on compute clusters. • cuDF: A drop in partial replacement for Pandas for use on GPUs. Developed by NVIDIA • Modin: A drop in GPU based replacement for Pandas. • Ray: A unified low level framework for scaling AI and Python applications. • RAPIDS: A set of libraries and APIs that runs on NVIDIA CUDA GPUs. It offers GPU-enabled substitutes for popular Python libraries, such as cuDF for Pandas, cuML for scikit-learn, and cuGraph for NetworkX. • Polars: A fast dataframe library implemented in Rust. (Runs in Python). • PySpark: The Python API for Spark that lets you harness the simplicity of Python and the power of Apache Spark.

GTK Cyber Apache Arrow • Apache Arrow is a standardized framework for developing data analytics applications that use columnar data. • Arrow can be used in python (PyArrow), Spark and many other languages. • Arrow is designed as a compliment to parquet format. • Main advantages are interoperability, speed and efficiency.
